citation: Chicago Board of Public Works. Tenth Annual Report to the Common Council, for the municipal year ending March 31, 1871. Chicago, 1871.
author: Chicago Board of Public Works
locator: Printed pages 17, 44, 48–49, 52 and 84, identified individually in chicago/pre_fire_v1/data/field_notebook_1871.json. Preserved bridge-table scan: chicago/pre_fire_v1/media/research/works-1871-p49.jpg. Street paving (T-3685): pp. 22-23 (wooden-block mileage, the worn Clark and Lake Street pavement, the principal-thoroughfare rule), pp. 25-27 (statement of assessments for wooden-block pavement, by warrant) and p. 37 (lineal feet of wooden-block and boulder pavement by division), read from the Internet Archive OCR text; transcribed in chicago/4d/data/context/1871/paving_1871.json. Fire hydrants (T-3805): pp. 8-9 (258 new in the year, 1,552 in the city at March 31, 1871), p. 61 (the shops' 335 new hydrants, eight of them triple), pp. 79-85 (the year's new hydrants by corner, by division), read from the Internet Archive OCR text (annualreportboa06workgoog_djvu.txt); transcribed in chicago/4d/data/research/street_furniture_1871.json.
rights_note: Original United States municipal publication dated 1871, public domain by age. This applies to the original report and faithful scan, not a modern annotated edition.
access_notes: Primary pages were inspected for the existing research notebook. The actual preserved page 49 bridge table was inspected again for this foundation on 2026-11-18. Fiscal year ends March 31; page 17 includes a July 15 addendum.
what_it_supplies: Bridge existence, construction years, reported lengths and March 31 traffic counts. Madison bridge is specified as all iron; others distinguish wooden or iron chords.
Contracted sidewalk work, park improvements and canal-opening chronology.
Wooden-block paving by street stretch (the warrants of 1870-71) and the city's wooden-block and boulder pavement by division, in lineal feet (T-3685).
The city's fire hydrants: their number at March 31, 1871, and each of the year's 258 new ones by street corner (T-3805).
what_it_does_not_supply: October 8 operating conditions, Sunday traffic volume, exact truss members, road widths or continuous pavement on every block.
note: Report-year evidence is brought forward to October 8 only as a bounded assumption. Reported bridge length is not a clear navigation opening. Erie and Twenty-second bridges were not in use at the March count; an October opening is not established here. Generic swing bridges do not claim exact engineering detail.
